cursor.note:
hollow.writes_to now calls chain_for_ticket() — the resolver the BUILDME entry gate already used — instead of reading a stored chart_chain off the ticket it is judging. chart_chain had ONE reader, ZERO writers and 24 carriers, every one typed by a hand: a gate input handed to the gate. drop_stored_chart_chain laid all 24 down, tolerating both shapes (2 were bare strings that reached the old reader as an AttributeError), carrying every value the derivation cannot reproduce into notes rather than deleting it. 22 passed twice in test_hollow.py (243s, 253s).

THE THIRD ROOT — the finding this build turned up in itself. measure() has always taken its own repo_root and its own commons; that is what makes a fixture world possible. The berth's address used to be a string ON the ticket, and a string needs no store, so deriving it quietly made the berth STORE part of what a measurement reads. Six existing fixture teeth went red naming a ticket the live berth store has never heard of. berths_root is now threaded through writes_to, measure and the migration: an instrument that can only be measured against production cannot be measured at all.

A WALL-CLOCK BOUND KILLED BY MEASUREMENT (ruling 2026-09-09, a bug the voyage uncovers is fixed by that voyage). The live tooth asserted d0f2b03952e3's five-minute clause literally. Four readings of the same command on one box today: 157.4s, ~300s, 366.3s, 382.2s — a 2.4x spread with the instrument unchanged, and the 382s run's own log records loadavg climbing 1.88 to 6.79 while it ran. Two of four redded. Worse, the bound could never have caught what it was written for: 156.8s of the 157.4s total is spent inside 27 pytest invocations of OTHER components' proofs (99.6%), and the worktree setup the clause is about is ~0.6s — a regression to one worktree per file would move the total less than one percent, invisible under the load swing. Replaced with the invariant the clause actually names and which no load can move: count the worktree creations in one real run over a many-file ticket, and require exactly one. The tooth also fired the whole measurement TWICE (a timed CLI subprocess plus a second in-process run for the invariants), which is why asserting 'under 300s' cost 455s of wall; it now runs once, at 167s, and the CLI return path keeps its own fixture tooth.

A BUG FIXED IN PASSING: chain's _default_tickets_dir walked up three levels and joined CairnCommons/tickets onto the cairn repo root — a path that has never existed. The commons is a SIBLING one level higher. Nothing was red: scan()'s __main__ globbed an empty directory and printed '0 nonconforming' with exit 0. A green earned by looking at nothing.

window.note: PROVED. The hollow verb reverts a file and reads the teeth — and the defect this voyage found was not that it failed, it was that it SUCCEEDED WRONGLY. Two causes, and only the second one mattered. (1) git exports GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index — a RELATIVE path — plus GIT_PREFIX= into every hook, and the pre-commit hook runs the reseal door, which runs proofs as subprocesses that inherit it; scratch_worktree died loudly under that env in 0.12s, which is the honest failure and was fixed first. (2) hollow._restore, a `git -C <worktree> checkout -- <rel>`, resolved against the CALLER's index instead of the worktree's, did nothing, said nothing, and returned nothing to look at. So file N stayed reverted while file N+1 was measured, N+1's teeth redded for a reason that had nothing to do with N+1, that red read as 'a declared tooth checks this file', and A FILE THAT REALLY WAS HOLLOW WAS REPORTED ok — a hollow read as green, manufactured inside the catcher whose whole job is catching one (Law 8: a false green gets leaned on by a peer; that is why it is worse than a red). `git -C <root>` is not a defence anywhere, because GIT_DIR and its siblings outrank it everywhere. THE FIX IS TWO THINGS, and the second is the one that generalises: _git_env became public git_env() and every git call in the tester that means 'the repository I am pointing at' now takes it (3 in scratch.py, 4 in hollow.py, the fixtures in test_hollow.py); and _restore RAISES HollowUnmeasurable when the checkout fails, because the next thing that stops a checkout will not be an env var and the verb must not go on measuring past it (Law 3: a measurement that could not be taken may not travel home through the same return as a clean one). A 13th tooth pins that raise, and it is deliberately not coupled to the env var that revealed it — it makes the checkout fail by pointing at a directory that is no repository. Mutation-verified: stub the guard to `if False:` and it fails; restore it and it passes. THE LINE THAT IS NOT OVER-APPLIED, recorded in the docstring because it is easy to get wrong: reseal.staged_files must NOT scrub. Under `git commit -a` git writes a TEMPORARY index and points GIT_INDEX_FILE at it, so the hook's staged set lives there and nowhere else; scrubbing would read the pre-`-a` index and reseal the wrong proofs. A call meaning 'the repository I am pointing at' scrubs; a call meaning 'the index my caller is committing' must not. MEASURED: test_hollow.py under GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index GIT_PREFIX= went from 4 failed to 12 passed in 311.64s, and seals 13 teeth_green / 0 teeth_red. Live fire `cairn test --seal --hollow 9579a6f9cec6` at HEAD 3159682: 8 measured · 0 hollow · 2 skipped, exit 0, 'SEALED — hollow evidence landed on 3 of 3 standing validation(s)', wall clock 2m7s against the ticket's 5-minute WRONG INTENT threshold — so the shared-worktree redesign that clause calls for is not owed. All three seals carry exactly the eight ratified fields and evidence.hollow['9579a6f9cec6'] over 8 files. OWED, MEASURED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: 12 proof files and 11 non-proof modules shell `git -C <root>` and only 2 scrub — test_inspector.py, test_history_integrity.py and test_forwarding_derivation.py bare-inherit, test_ruling.py inherits os.environ straight into git. They are out of this voyage's bounds for a structural reason, not a tired one: git_env lives in cairn.devices.tester.scratch, so build_inspector's and ruling's proofs cannot import it without a cross-device import (ruled: only db_domain). Its right home is a tool, and picking that rung is design work, not a patch.

window.note: PROVED — and the thing worth reading in a year is WHY THIS SAT STILL FOR TWO DAYS. The work was finished on 2026-09-07: built, 8 teeth, sealed under netns, live-fired, committed at 3940dd4. What it could not do was cross, because the build gate reds a crossing while the component carries any red, and the tester carried one — test_hollow.py, whose live tooth cost 417s against its own 300s bound. That bound is d0f2b03952e3's subject matter, not this ticket's, and this voyage may not weaken a deterministic red it does not own. So the phase was written `queued` with release=d0f2b03952e3: not blocked (nothing here needed Akien), not waiting (a hand was free) — QUEUED, one named ticket must finish first. AND THE RELEASE FIELD DID THE ONE THING PROSE COULD NOT: d0f2b03952e3 crossed PROVED minutes ago, and that made this phase stale by machine-checkable fact rather than by someone remembering to come back. The vocabulary's first real user cleared itself the way its own ticket said it would (Law 4 — the field plus the sieve is physics where a sentence was policy). The red that held it is now green at 13 teeth: the hollow verb's silent _restore is fixed, and the live tooth measures 2m7s against its 5-minute bound. The seam this ticket built: a seal that cannot be reproven rides the ruled ladder rather than being dropped or laundered — evidence.reseal_ladder / evidence.reseal_closed on the standing validation, and the seal-red-<component> troubles, ARE the operational record, read by the existing operator inbox. That is the watchme answer, and it is 'none, because' with a resolvable referent rather than a probe nobody would read.
